fact: 1915年5月7日卢西塔尼亚号被击沉、1198人死亡（含128名美国公民）后，美国于5月13日向柏林发出照会，指德国潜艇战「远远超出常规作战方法」。5月10日威尔逊在费城演说中称「一个人可以骄傲到不屑于动手」。事件引发针对德裔与德资企业的骚动，但美国当时仍维持中立。

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica, Lusitania
sources.quote: The loss of the liner and so many of its passengers, including 128 U.S. citizens, aroused a wave of indignation in the United States, and it was fully expected that a declaration of war would follow, but the U.S. government clung to its policy of neutrality. ... On May 13, 1915, the U.S. government sent a note to Berlin expressing an indictment of the principles on which the submarine war was being fought. The note was written by Secretary of State William Jennings Bryan

sources.title: Alpha History, World War I timeline
sources.quote: May 10th: Woodrow Wilson tells a Philadelphia audience that "there is such a thing as a man being too proud to fight". ... The incident causes outrage in several nations, particularly the US and Britain. Several attacks on Germans and German-owned businesses are reported.

fact: 1915年8月19日，英国客轮阿拉伯号（Arabic）在爱尔兰外海被德国潜艇击沉，死者中包括两名美国人。在美国抗议下，德国于8月30日（一说9月18日）停止不经警告击沉客船，此即「阿拉伯号承诺」；无限制潜艇战在秋季暂停。

sources.title: Historic UK, World War 1 Timeline – 1915
sources.quote: 19 Aug The British passenger liner Arabic is torpedoed by a German U-boat off the coast of Ireland. Among the dead are two Americans. ... 30 Aug In response to American demands, Germany stops sinking ships without warning.

sources.title: Alpha History, World War I timeline
sources.quote: September 18th: Under pressure from the United States, Berlin calls an indefinite halt to its campaign of unrestricted submarine warfare.

fact: 美国的中立财政政策在1915年转向：1914年国务卿布赖恩反对向交战国提供贷款，1915年8月21日财政部长麦卡杜致信威尔逊，指出对协约国的军需出口带来繁荣、若不开放贷款则无法持续；9月6日国务卿兰辛持同样意见；9月8日威尔逊同意放贷。此后对协约国的正式贷款迅速展开。

sources.title: Barnes, The United States and the First World War（引 McAdoo 1915年8月21日致威尔逊函、Lansing 9月6日函）
sources.quote: On August 21, 1915, McAdoo wrote a long letter to President Wilson, pointing out that great prosperity had come to the country as a result of the sale of munitions to the Allies, but that this prosperity could not continue unless we financed it through open loans to the Allies ... On September 6, 1915, Secretary Lansing argued similarly in a letter to President Wilson ... On September 8, 1915, Wilson assented to loans

fact: 1915年1月（一说2月15日），J.P.摩根公司成为英国政府在美国的唯一采购代理，法国随后签订类似合同。同年9月，英国派雷丁勋爵率英法财政委员会赴美，9月28日宣布由摩根公司牵头的辛迪加与英法政府达成5亿美元贷款：五年期5%债券，面值100美元起，向公众按98美元发行，辛迪加按96美元承销，投资者收益率约5.5%。这是此前华尔街史上最大的单笔外国贷款。

sources.title: Commercial and Financial Chronicle, 1915-10-02, Vol. 101 No. 2623（FRASER 全文）
sources.quote: the completion of the negotiations and agreement upon the terms ... a loan to the British and the French Governments ... The $500,000,000 is to consist of 5% five-year bonds ... the bonds will be issued to the public at 98, yielding approximately 5 1/2% to the investor ... This syndicate ... will contract to purchase the loan from the two Governments at 96.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Anglo-French Financial Commission
sources.quote: The group arrived in New York on 10 September, and were met by J. P. Morgan Jr., who had been designated as Britain's sole purchasing agent in the United States in January 1915 ... On 28 September 1915 it was announced that the syndicate, led by J.P. Morgan & Co., had reached a credit agreement with the British and French governments. The loan was for $500,000,000, at that point by far the largest single loan in financial history.

fact: 伯利恒钢铁（Bethlehem Steel）普通股价格在1915年内由约47美元升至460美元，全年最高600美元；另有记载称1907年为8美元、1913年30美元、1915年600美元。该公司1916年利润逾6100万美元，超过其此前八年销售额总和。

sources.title: The Morning Call, Forging America: The History of Bethlehem Steel – Chapter 3
sources.quote: The price of its common stock had risen from $8 a share in 1907, to $30 a share in 1913, to $600 a share in 1915 and to a peak of $700 a share in 1916. ... "The most remarkable year in Bethlehem's history was 1916," Hessen notes in his book. "Its earnings in that year — over $61 million — exceeded all the gross sales of the first eight, prewar years that the company had been under Schwab's direction."

sources.title: Economic Indicator Services, Land of oranges and speculators（引 Fridson 与 《The Great Game》）
sources.quote: The Bethlehem Steel stock price went from 47 to 460 (dollars), with a high at 600 during the year.

fact: 与欧洲交战国相比，1915年美国消费者物价几乎未动：1914年12月至1915年12月涨幅至多2%，纽约市的统计为1.97%；批发物价指数（1913年7月—1914年6月=100）从1914年7月的99升到1915年12月的106，涨幅集中在军工所需原料。零售食品价格上涨更晚，到1916年6月才升至112（1913=100）。

sources.title: The High Cost of Living: Respite and Upsurge, 1915 to Early 1917（Palgrave/Springer 专著章节，引 BLS Bulletin 296/300）
sources.quote: The wholesale price index (July 1913–June 1914 = 100) rose from 99 in July 1914 to 106 in December 1915 ... Consumer prices rose at most 2 percent between December 1914 and December 1915. ... By June 1916, the BLS index of retail food prices (1913 = 100) had risen to 112.

sources.title: Changes in Cost of Living and Prices 1914 to 1920（美国劳工统计局数据汇编，Internet Archive 全文）
sources.quote: New York, N. Y....1.97 ... Percentage of increase from December, 1914, to—December 1915

fact: 1915年美国军火出口从1914年的4000万美元跃升至3.3亿美元（1916年为12.9亿美元）。伯利恒钢铁的未完成订单从1913年底的2486.5万美元增至1914年底4651.3万美元、1915年底1.75432亿美元。杜邦在1915年把无烟火药价格翻倍，年利润从500万美元升至8200万美元。

sources.title: Ferdinand Lundberg, America's 60 Families（1937）节选，WWI Resource Centre
sources.quote: Whereas unfilled orders of the Bethlehem Steel Corporation at the end of 1913 were Only $24,865,000, at the end of 1914 they stood at $46,513,000 and at the end of 1915 at $175,432,000. Munitions exports in 1914 totaled $40,000,000; in 1915 they were $330,000,000, in 1916, $1,290,000,000.

sources.title: Encyclopedia.com, Profiteering（引 Jennifer D. Keene）
sources.quote: Du Pont, which manufactured smokeless gunpowder, doubled its price in 1915 and saw its annual profits skyrocket from $5 million to $82 million. The J. P. Morgan banking firm earned $30 million for its work as purchasing agent for the British.

fact: 1915年，伯利恒钢铁替英国建造的20艘潜艇在9月前全部下水。为规避美国的中立法，其中10艘的部件运到加拿大蒙特利尔的维克斯船厂组装，公司对外称运往加拿大的是桥梁用钢；德国大使就此向美方抗议，公司则主张这些部件须在加拿大进一步加工、不属禁运的军舰部件。伯利恒由此获得约400万美元的利润与赶工奖金。

sources.title: The Morning Call, Forging America: The History of Bethlehem Steel – Chapter 3
sources.quote: All 20 submarines were launched by September 1915, and Bethlehem Steel got $4 million in profits and bonuses for speedy delivery. ... Bethlehem sent two of its shipyard presidents and 500 workers and supervisors to Montreal, where they were sworn to secrecy. Executives told the press that the steel they were sending across the border would help replace bridges destroyed in Europe ... Technically, the company argued, they weren't prohibited parts for a war vessel because they had to be further fabricated in Montreal before the subs were completed.
